actions: Retried discovery of Zenodo software artifact 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 through DOI, Zenodo-index search, Nature/PMC/OpenReview references and public web mirrors. The peer-reviewed article still explicitly states that all simulation/analysis code is deposited there, but the current transport did not expose the record file list or downloadable archive; no code execution or exact replication was claimed.
Searched exact-title/DOI/author terms for non-author reruns, failures, forks or citations. No clear independent PRG reproduction was found in the accessible public results.

Extracted version-of-record source details needed for a source-derived ablation: 512-neuron vanilla RNN, tau=2, leaky ReLU recurrent update plus per-step layer normalization, T=100 synthetic clips, 12 direction classes, sparse Bernoulli input noise p=0.01, truncated BPTT with Adam 1e-4; the controlled-representation experiment reports direction+position entanglement at participation-ratio dimensionality 7.7 while direction-only is approximately 2.11.

Ran a deliberately cheap source-derived causal control that does not claim exact PRG reproduction. Synthetic 2-D motion trajectories encoded 12 directions over 20 time steps with Gaussian observation noise. Training data contained a strong spurious correlation between direction and absolute starting position; test data removed that correlation. Compared the same small GRU on raw versus trajectory-centered input and a non-recurrent linear classifier on the centered trajectory. Five independent training seeds, 5,000 train and 2,000 test trajectories per condition.

The raw GRU fit IID training structure well (92.92% mean accuracy) but collapsed under position-shift to 9.67%, approximately chance for 12 classes. Subtracting the first position before the same GRU restored 92.78% under the position shift, 90.02% with 30% frame-drop/hold corruption, and 82.71% with 60% frame-drop/hold. A centered non-recurrent linear trajectory classifier reached 99.73%, 97.45%, and 90.03% on those same shifted/corrupted conditions respectively.

This source-derived control isolates a design factor rather than reproducing the paper: when nuisance position is explicitly removed, transfer survives without an attractor or recurrence. Recurrence alone does not prevent shortcut use under entangled position-direction training statistics. This strengthens the hypothesis that low-dimensional primitive isolation/disentanglement is at least one sufficient contributor in the simple synthetic regime, while leaving the peer-reviewed real DVS/RGB attractor-transfer claim unresolved.

prg_peer_reviewed.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation
verified_source_facts: Direction RNN uses 12 directions and T=100 moving-bar clips with sparse Bernoulli noise p=0.01.
RNN hidden state is leaky recurrent ReLU with tau=2 followed by per-step layer normalization; optimization uses truncated BPTT and Adam lr=1e-4.
Direction-only hidden activity is reported at participation-ratio effective dimension approximately 2.11.

Controlled mixed direction+position pretraining is reported at effective dimension 7.7 and markedly reduced real-task transfer/perturbation robustness despite comparable synthetic pretraining decoding.
Methods define the custom RGB dataset as 14 effective categories after merging two indistinguishable level-0 cases, preserving the previously noted Results/Methods category-count inconsistency.

artifact_transport.interpretation: Do not treat code as absent. Exact seeds, few-shot sampling, saved train/test splits and Supplementary-Fig-4 generation code remain pending artifact access.

source_derived_ablation.purpose: Test whether explicit primitive isolation can explain robustness independently of recurrent-attractor dynamics in a cheap motion domain.

design.train_nuisance: absolute start position strongly correlated with direction
design.test_shift: start position sampled independently of direction
design.frame_dropout: dropped frames held at previous observation
models: same GRU after subtracting first position from all timesteps
multinomial linear classifier on centered flattened trajectory

scope: Inputs are 2-D motion trajectories, not paper-format binary videos, DVS streams or the custom RGB dataset.
The nuisance correlation was intentionally constructed to stress representation entanglement; it is not claimed to match the paper's training distribution.
Trajectory centering is an explicit hand-designed invariance and therefore a stronger prior than the paper's learned direction module.
The linear control is not parameter matched to the paper's 512-neuron RNN.

Result supports primitive isolation as a sufficient mechanism in this synthetic regime, not that recurrence/attractor dynamics are unnecessary for real video transfer or temporal robustness generally.

evidence_added_this_run: Source-derived nuisance-shift ablation: raw GRU 9.67% versus centered same-GRU 92.78% and centered non-recurrent linear 99.73% after removal of a train-time direction-position shortcut; 5 seeds.
With position shift plus 60% frame-drop/hold, centered GRU retained 82.71% and centered linear 90.03%, while raw GRU remained 9.33%.

Version-of-record controlled representation result independently reports that a mixed direction+position representation has effective dimensionality 7.7 and markedly reduced real transfer robustness versus the approximately-2.11-dimensional direction-only representation.
candidate_update.interpretation: The strongest current mechanistic hypothesis is low-dimensional physical-primitive isolation/disentanglement plus temporal robustness, not recurrence/continuous-attractor dynamics alone. The peer-reviewed study still supplies real DVS/RGB evidence and dynamic perturbation evidence that this source-derived control does not reproduce.
